articles.headline: McVay: Rams coaches will 'learn' from incident with Eagles fans
articles.description: Rams coach Sean McVay says his assistant coaches will learn from their viral interaction with Eagles fans during Sunday's win over Philadelphia.
articles.headlineJa: マクベイ：ラムズのコーチ陣はイーグルスファンとの騒動から「学ぶ」ことになる
articles.descriptionJa: ラムズのショーン・マクベイ監督は、日曜日のフィラデルフィア戦での勝利の際、イーグルスのファンとのやり取りが拡散した件について、アシスタントコーチ陣はこれを教訓にすると語った。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES  -- After the Rams' comeback victory over the Eagles in Philadelphia on Sunday, several videos surfaced of some Los Angeles assistant coaches interacting with the home fans from the coach's booth.

In the videos, posted on the social media platform X on Sunday night, an assistant coach appears to bang on the glass and then gesture at Eagles fans sitting in the stands below the booth after the Rams' go-ahead touchdown. One video shows a cup and then a water bottle thrown from the stands at the glass windows of the booth.

Rams head coach Sean McVay said he and the assistant coaches talked about the incident, saying, "We'll be better in those situations."

The Rams came back after trailing 20-10 with 8 minutes and 17 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter. According to ESPN Analytics, the Eagles' win probability peaked at 97.4% at that moment, with Philadelphia on the Los Angeles two yard line. The Rams scored touchdowns with 3:59 and 1:45 remaining to win the game.

McVay acknowledged he has been in a similar situation in Washington when he was calling plays from the booth, saying, "you get excited and emotional."

"We'll learn from that," McVay said. "We'll be better. Those fans are really into it, but I know that we want to make sure that we're representing the class and just the calm steadiness that we want to have while also being emotionally into it. And there's ways that we can have that reflected.

"We did talk about it and that won't be an issue moving forward."

articles.headline: NBA testing smart basketballs, wrist wearables in preseason
articles.description: The NBA is experimenting with smart basketballs and wrist wearables for officials in select preseason games in order to collect data on the review process.
articles.headlineJa: NBA、プレシーズンでスマートボールとリストバンド型ウェアラブルを試験導入
articles.descriptionJa: NBAは、ビデオ判定プロセスに関するデータを収集するため、一部のプレシーズンゲームにおいて、スマートボールと審判用のリストバンド型ウェアラブルを試験的に導入している。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The NBA is experimenting with two pieces of technology in the leadup to the season, the league announced Monday.

Select exhibition games will include a smart basketball that has a Bluetooth sensor in it and can collect data for future use in real-time officiating decisions. The league said the information from the Wilson-developed "connected" balls will be for research only and not affect calls made during those games.

Officials in select games will also use wrist wearables to communicate with the replay center in designated situations, including replay reviews, scoring changes and clock malfunctions.

The wearables went through what the NBA called a successful pilot program during the summer league. The technology will not extend into the regular season.

articles.headline: Sources: Eagles RB Tank Bigsby to have surgery, headed to IR
articles.description: Eagles running back Tank Bigsby sustained a core muscle injury Sunday that requires surgery, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者によると、イーグルスのRBタンク・ビッグスビーが手術へ、IR入りへ
articles.descriptionJa: NFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポート氏が伝えたところによると、イーグルスのランニングバック、タンク・ビッグスビーは体幹部の筋肉の負傷により手術を受けることになった。
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles' running back depth chart is in flux after Sunday's game.

In addition to the hamstring injury suffered by starter Saquon Barkley against the Los Angeles Rams, his backup, Tank Bigsby, sustained a core muscle injury that requires surgery, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Bigsby is headed to injured reserve with the hope that he'll be back in six weeks or less, the sources told Rapoport.

Earlier Monday, coach Nick Sirianni said, "We'll see" when asked if Barkley will be available to play Sunday when the Eagles face the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

articles.headline: Bills CB Maxwell Hairston sorry for skipping media, addresses struggles
articles.description: A day after skipping out on the media, Bills cornerback Maxwell Hairston held an impromptu news conference to apologize and provide context for his early-season struggles.
articles.headlineJa: ビルズのCBマクスウェル・ヘアストン、メディア取材回避を謝罪、不調について言及
articles.descriptionJa: メディア取材を避けた翌日、ビルズのコーナーバック、マクスウェル・ヘアストンは急遽記者会見を開き、謝罪するとともに、シーズン序盤の不調の背景について説明した。
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Buffalo Bills cornerback Maxwell Hairston held an impromptu news conference Monday to apologize for his behavior after the Bills' 29-26 loss Sunday and give context to his lackluster performance as criticism of his play heightens through four weeks.

Hairston, the Bills' first-round pick in 2025, allowed a pair of touchdowns in one-on-one coverage against New England Patriots receiver Romeo Doubs in Sunday's loss. After the game, Hairston refused to speak to media about his play as Bills coach Joe Brady was facing down questions about whether Hairston should be benched.

"Feeling very emotional, I let my emotions get the best of me, and I didn't want to say something I might have regretted," Hairston said Monday. "You live and you learn. ... That's kind of immature, and I'm better than that. So I wanted to get that out of the way."

Hairston sums up his recent struggles by explaining he needs to be better with his eyes. He's staring down quarterbacks instead of receivers and thinking about the ball instead of the route. That makes it easier for receivers to finish at the point of attack, since Hairston is a split second behind when his eyes are in the wrong spot.

The Bills' coverage issues extend beyond Hairston. Buffalo ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game, and only the Detroit Lions are allowing more first downs per game.

Hairston, Dee Alford and Christian Benford all rank among the bottom 10 cornerbacks in the league (minimum 100 coverage snaps) per Pro Football Focus coverage grade.

But Hairston is the one catching heat, in large part because his poor play is also coming across as lackluster effort. With 55 seconds left in Sunday's game, Hairston had an angle on Patriots tight end Hunter Henry on a third-and-10 completion that could've been stopped short and forced a punt to give Josh Allen and the Bills' offense one more chance to tie the score with a field goal. But Hairston wasn't going full speed, and Henry easily cleared the first down.

Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said Hairston's effort clearly wasn't good enough on that play and said Hairston's "emotions are getting the best of him."

"I have to be in control of my emotions within the game," Hairston said in response. "It comes with learning, experiencing certain stuff. I have to be better in that aspect."

Despite all this, Brady remains steadfast that benching Hairston is not in the cards. Hairston will start for Buffalo on "Monday Night Football" against the Los Angeles Rams this week, and Brady is already manifesting a big bounce-back game for his cornerback.

"Max Hairston's going to make a play this week, and you guys are going to be asking me questions like, 'Oh man, what was it like seeing him respond from the previous game?'" Brady said.

articles.headline: Sources: Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton expected back in 12-16 weeks
articles.description: Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton is expected back from a dislocated left ankle injury within 12 to 16 weeks, sources told NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者によると、チーフスのWRタイクアン・ソーントンは12〜16週間での復帰見込み
articles.descriptionJa: NFLネットワークが伝えた関係者の話によると、チーフスのワイドレシーバー、タイクアン・ソーントンは、左足首の脱臼による怪我から12〜16週間以内に復帰する見込みだ。
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton is expected to return before the end of the season after he suffered a serious ankle injury in the fourth quarter of his team's 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

After extensive tests Monday, Thornton is expected back within 12 to 16 weeks from his dislocated left ankle, sources told Rapoport. Thornton will undergo surgery on the ankle this week, and the Chiefs hope he can return by the end of the regular season or the playoffs.

The injury came after he made a key 55-yard catch. Thornton, a four-year veteran, was forced to exit Allegiant Stadium on crutches.

 

"It sucks that he hurt his ankle on that play, but it was a big play for us," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said after Sunday's game. "It helped us go get the win. It's tough because those guys put in so much work. I was in that spot last year. One play can change your season. You hope for the best, but at the same time you want to show him support. I know how it is when you're in that position, and it's like the world is closing in on you. He's one of the best teammates I've ever had."

One avenue to address Thornton's absence would be a reunion with free agent Tyreek Hill. Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he plans to begin negotiating a deal for the veteran receiver with multiple teams Monday. The Chiefs are in the mix and have maintained contact with Hill.

Thornton wasn't the only hit to the Chiefs' wide receiver room Sunday. Fellow wideout Rashee Rice left the win in the first quarter because of a right hamstring injury. He recorded a 7-yard reception but stumbled and pulled up while trying to gain yards after the catch, ending the play by going out of bounds. Rice tried to stay in the game, but he headed to the locker room before halftime after a lengthy chat with team trainer Rick Burkholder.

Reid didn't seem too concerned about Rice in his postgame news conference Sunday. The veteran was held out for the rest of the game as a precaution.

Sunday was the best game in Thornton's career. He led the Chiefs with five catches for a career-high 111 receiving yards and two touchdowns as they improved to 4-0.

Through the first four weeks, Rice and Thornton have been Kansas City's best receivers, combining to make 24 catches on 31 targets for 409 yards and three touchdowns.

articles.headline: Hornets guard Coby White to sit preseason after calf strain
articles.description: Hornets guard Coby White suffered a left calf strain during training camp and will miss the remainder of preseason, the team announced Monday.
articles.headlineJa: ホーネッツのガード、コービー・ホワイトがふくらはぎの筋挫傷によりプレシーズン欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: ホーネッツは月曜日、ガードのコービー・ホワイトがトレーニングキャンプ中に左ふくらはぎの筋挫傷を負い、プレシーズンの残りの試合を欠場することを発表した。
articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets guard Coby White suffered a left calf strain during training camp and will miss the remainder of preseason, the team announced Monday.

White, 26, signed a three-year, $74 million contract with Charlotte over the summer and is expected to play a large role this season after the LaMelo Ball trade left a void in the backcourt.

White joins second-year guard Kon Knueppel on the sideline for the remainder of preseason. Knueppel suffered a left hamstring strain earlier in training camp.

The Hornets acquired White from the Chicago Bulls in February and he went on to have a strong finish to the season with his new team. He was the hero in the team's play-in victory over the Miami Heat, scoring 19 points and hitting the turnaround 3 late in regulation to force overtime.

The Hornets' preseason begins Tuesday night while their regular season opens on the road in Brooklyn on October 21.

articles.headline: James, Embiid, Maxey sit out 76ers' preseason opener vs. Knicks
articles.description: LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey will sit out the 76ers' preseason opener against the Knicks on Monday night.
articles.headlineJa: ジェームズ、エンビード、マクシーがニックス戦の76ersプレシーズン開幕戦を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜夜に行われるニックス戦の76ersプレシーズン開幕戦には、レブロン・ジェームズ、ジョエル・エンビード、タイリース・マクシーは出場しない。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- LeBron James and Joel Embiid are among the healthy inactives for the Philadelphia 76ers in their preseason opener Monday night against the NBA champion New York Knicks.

All-Star guard Tyrese Maxey also will sit out. Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe are the lone regular starters in the lineup.

The Sixers went 45-37 last season and were swept in the second round of the playoffs by the Knicks.

James signed a free-agent deal with the Sixers over the summer. He is a 22-time All-Star, a 21-time All-NBA selection, a four-time Most Valuable Player, a four-time NBA Finals MVP, a three-time All-Star Game MVP and a member of the NBA's 75th anniversary team.

James, Embiid and the full healthy roster played in a public scrimmage on Saturday on the 76ers' home court.

articles.headline: Pat Surtain II out with an ankle injury: How will the Denver Broncos adjust?
articles.description: While Surtain was able to avoid a long-term, season-ending injury, the loss of him and Riley Moss puts the Broncos in a short-term bind.
articles.headlineJa: パット・サーテイン2世が足首の負傷で離脱：デンバー・ブロンコスはどう対応するか？
articles.descriptionJa: サーテインは長期離脱やシーズン絶望の事態は免れたものの、彼とライリー・モスの離脱により、ブロンコスは当面の苦境に立たされている。
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Before the season began, Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II penned a first-person offering in the Players' Tribune that closed with the phrase "Let me just tell you straight up: You're making a big mistake if you're trying to write off Denver."

Less than a month later, Surtain's season, the Broncos' defensive plan and the team's overall fortunes have taken a hit -- though not as big of a hit as originally feared. Surtain, who left Sunday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers just before halftime, could miss multiple games with a right ankle injury, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. But even though Surtain avoided a season-ending injury, even a missed series would impact the Broncos, who have an AFC West matchup Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers in SoFi Stadium followed by a short turnaround for a Thursday night affair against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Surtain is a two-time first-team All Pro and was the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year in 2024. And his status as the game's best cornerback and one of the linchpins of the Broncos' defensive plan means the proverbial "next man up" will have one of the most difficult assignments in the NFL.

"Of course, [on Monday] and throughout the week, really we'll stay away from any updates,'' Broncos coach Sean Payton said Monday. "Guys were all in getting work and rehabbing."

Surtain's absence, no matter how long, would impact how the Broncos construct their pass rush and coverage plans along with their ability to match a cornerback on the league's best wide receivers as often as they do with him. With fellow outside cornerback Riley Moss also leaving Sunday's game with a rib injury shortly after Surtain went down, the Broncos' pass defense could look vastly different in the weeks ahead.

"You'll go 16 weeks, and that might happen once every two years, but you have to be ready," coach Sean Payton said of the timing of the two CB injuries. "It affects if you can get into dime ... it may take you out of some packages."

On a first-and-10 play from the 49ers' 42-yard line with 30 seconds left in the first half, 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy completed a 4-yard pass to Christian McCaffrey. But away from the play, Surtain pivoted in coverage and began to hop on his left foot, keeping his right foot off the ground. He was taken to the locker room and evaluated, then underwent additional tests Sunday night and Monday by the team's medical staff.

Jahdae Barron (2025 first-round pick) and Kris Abrams-Draine (2024 fifth-round pick) played outside corner for the remainder of Sunday's game. They held their own in most individual matchups with the 49ers' wide receivers in the 24-14 loss, but Purdy accumulated 129 of his 218 passing yards in the second half, along with both of his touchdown passes.

articles.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins day-to-day with adductor injury, coach says
articles.description: Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins is considered day-to-day with an adductor issue he suffered toward the end of Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
articles.headlineJa: ベンガルズのWRティー・ヒギンズ、内転筋の負傷で経過観察の状態、コーチが語る
articles.descriptionJa: ベンガルズのワイドレシーバー、ティー・ヒギンズは、日曜日のジャクソンビル・ジャガーズ戦（22-17で敗戦）の終盤に負った内転筋のトラブルにより、日単位での状態確認が必要な状況にある。
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- Bengals coach Zac Taylor delivered a bit of optimistic injury news Monday.

Wide receiver Tee Higgins is considered day-to-day with an adductor issue he suffered toward the end of Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Higgins tried to play through the injury on Cincinnati's final drive of the game but ultimately wasn't able to continue.

However, Taylor's prognosis opens the door for the seventh-year player to suit up for the team's upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins.

With star receiver Ja'Marr Chase out for most of yesterday's game with a concussion, Higgins had one of the best outings of his career -- 11 catches on 16 targets for 157 yards.

"Obviously [with] the game he had and the performances he's had for us in the past, any time you can get him it's great," Taylor said. "So we'll just see where he's at this week."

Taylor said the team will develop Higgins' rehab and preparation plan starting on Wednesday, which is the first practice day of the week.

Cincinnati will also have to see how Chase progresses as well. He is currently in concussion protocol, Taylor said, following a hit he sustained early in the second quarter.

Jaguars cornerback Jarrian Jones pulled Chase to the ground by his facemask, drawing a personal foul penalty. As Chase was heading to the turf, Jaguars linebacker Ventrell Miller hit Chase near the neck area. Chase did not return to the game. The injuries to Higgins and Chase will limit an already-depleted group. Cincinnati wide receiver Andrei Iosivas is on injured reserve while he recovers from thumb surgery, while rookie wideout Colbie Young is dealing with a left knee injury.

Taylor did not indicate when Young could return but suggested the outlook is better than initially believed.

"He's coming along faster than I would have initially thought," Taylor said. "I think that's the good news on it."

But as things stand, that leaves two healthy receivers on the team's 53-player roster -- Dohnte Meyers, a first-year NFL player who had a career-high 82 yards on Sunday; Mitch Tinsley, who was with the Bengals last season and returned last week after being signed from the Houston Texans' practice squad. Tinsley had three catches on seven targets for 49 yards.

Taylor mentioned rookie Noah Thomas and veteran Jordan Moore as potential options off the practice squad if needed for the team's road game against Miami (0-4).

Cincinnati (2-2) is looking to break a two-game losing streak before entering its bye week.

articles.headline: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns not expecting contract extension soon
articles.description: Karl-Anthony Towns says the chances "don't look good" for him getting a new extension with the Knicks before the start of the regular season.
articles.headlineJa: ニックスのカール＝アンソニー・タウンズ、早期の契約延長は見込んでいない
articles.descriptionJa: カール＝アンソニー・タウンズは、レギュラーシーズン開幕前にニックスとの新たな契約延長を得られる可能性は「低そうだ」と語った。
articles.body:
The New York Knicks take the court for their first preseason game Monday night, but one of the key players in last season's championship run remains at odds with the team over a contract extension.

"It don't look good," Karl-Anthony Towns said Monday of getting a new contract in place before the start of the regular season.

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million. He is due $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for next season.

Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that the Knicks' latest offer to Towns was a four-year deal worth approximately $200 million.

A six-time All-Star, Towns was a catalyst for the Knicks' playoff run last season, averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists as New York won the title in a five-game Finals over the San Antonio Spurs.

Does that mean the Knicks should reward Towns for his hand in ending a 53-year title drought?

"No s---, Sherlock," Towns said. "I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys [reporters] think I have something else to prove."

Knicks owner James Dolan has said the team will not go into the second spending apron, which means tough decisions will need to be made. New York did not re-sign backup center Mitchell Robinson this offseason. Robinson, who was the longest-tenured Knick on last year's team, signed with the Boston Celtics.

Towns said that he's aware of the challenges of maintaining a championship core but that in his estimation the team has not done enough to compromise.

"Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said. "None of those things have come close to happening."

Information from ESPN's Vincent Goodwill was used in this report.

Hawkins, Grizzlies mutually agree to part ways

The Memphis Grizzlies and guard Jordan Hawkins have agreed to part ways via waivers, allowing the 2023 lottery pick to find a new home in free agency, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

articles.description: England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford nearly caused a crash with two other cars during a bout of careless driving in his £200,000 Lamborghini supercar, a court has heard.
articles.headlineJa: ジョーダン・ピックフォード、譲れの標識を無視し衝突寸前、法廷で明らかに
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドのゴールキーパー、ジョーダン・ピックフォードが、20万ポンドのスーパーカー、ランボルギーニを不注意に運転し、他の2台の車との衝突事故を引き起こしかけたことが法廷で明らかにされた。
articles.body:
England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford nearly caused a crash with two other cars during a bout of careless driving in his £200,000 Lamborghini supercar, a court has heard.

The 32-year-old was pulled over by police after ignoring a give-way sign, forcing two cars to slam on the brakes, and then speeding off into the distance.

The incident happened in the upmarket Cheshire town of Knutsford on April 14, sparking a criminal prosecution for driving without due care or attention.

Pickford, who has 336 appearances for Everton and 92 England caps, has pleaded guilty to the charge and requested a court hearing to explain his mitigation.

According to court documents, Pc Cecil Ricardo, from Cheshire Police, said he had just left the station when he saw Pickford's blue Lamborghini Urus complete with personalised number plates.

"I was stationary on Bexton Road, Knutsford, waiting for traffic signals to turn green," he wrote.

"I then witnessed a blue Lamborghini Urus driving along Princess Street.

"It reached the junction with Toft Road, completely ignored the give way lines and pulled onto Toft Road causing two vehicles to slam on their brakes to avoid a collision.

"The Lamborghini then sped down Toft Road, Knutsford."

Pc Ricardo said he activated his lights and siren to set off in pursuit of the Lamborghini, noticing he was driving at 50mph while the Lamborghini "was still pulling away." 

"The speed limit on that stretch of Toft Road, Knutsford, is 30mph," he noted.

The officer said Pickford appeared to notice the chasing police car and pulled over.

Pickford pleaded guilty in writing in the Single Justice Procedure and told Warrington Magistrates Court: "I would like to attend court to put forward my mitigation."

His case was formally adjourned last week until a hearing at Chester Magistrates' Court on Dec. 7.

Pickford, who started his career at Sunderland before loan spells at six clubs including Burton, Bradford and Preston, has featured for England at the 2018, 2022 and 2026 World Cups, and was in goal for the country's Euro 2020 and 2024 final appearances.

articles.headline: JJ Gabriel representatives demanded game time at Manchester United - sources
articles.description: Representatives of JJ Gabriel demanded that the teenager played at least 20 minutes in games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth before beginning talks about signing a scholarship with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: JJ・ガブリエルの代理人がマンチェスター・ユナイテッドでの出場時間を要求 - 関係者談
articles.descriptionJa: JJ・ガブリエルの代理人が、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドとの奨学金契約に関する交渉を開始する前に、サバFK、ブライトン、ボーンマス戦で少なくとも20分間の出場を要求したと、関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
Representatives of JJ Gabriel demanded that the teenager played at least 20 minutes in games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth before beginning talks about signing a scholarship with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN.

Gabriel, 15, has not trained with United since walking out on the club ahead of their Carabao Cup tie with Brighton on Sept. 16.

He is pictured in United's squad photo, which was released on Monday. However, the image was taken nearly a month ago and sources have told ESPN there is little sign of a reconciliation with the club.

Gabriel's representatives believe certain promises made by Man United have also been broken, sources told ESPN.

Gabriel's representatives have been approached by ESPN for comment.

Gabriel, who turns 16 on Tuesday, was due to make his first team debut against Brighton before representatives demanded United cancel his registration over a row about his playing time.

He made his first-team debut in a preseason friendly against Atlético Madrid in the summer, but was omitted from the squad for the Champions League.

Sources have told ESPN that representatives told United he must play at least 20 minutes against Sabah, Brighton and in the Premier League fixture against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Oct. 25 before entering discussions over a scholarship.

Gabriel could have signed a pre-agreement from his 16th birthday on Oct. 6.

With it looking increasingly likely that Gabriel will leave, United, according to sources, are prepared to take legal action if there is evidence of other clubs approaching Gabriel outside of the rules.

They have yet to receive a formal enquiry.

A number of clubs have been linked with a move including Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Despite a breakdown in relations with Gabriel's camp, sources have told ESPN that they continue to believe Old Trafford is the best place for him to develop.

Club officials have made a number of attempts to check on his well-being since he stopped reporting for training.

- Barcelona sporting director: No interest in Man United's JJ Gabriel

- Rooney: 'Disappointing' if 'top player' JJ Gabriel leaves Man United

- Why Man United's wantaway wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, is so highly rated

Sources insist they have made every effort to show he has a pathway to the first team, including assigning coaches and specialist staff -- who usually only work with senior players -- to ensure he's prepared for the demands of professional football.

United also accepted a demand from Gabriel to be given the No.77 squad number for this season and petitioned the Premier League on his behalf to allow him to have the name "Gabriel JR" on his shirt.

Sources close to United insist they have prioritised Gabriel's well-being throughout his time at Old Trafford.

There has been a feeling internally that his representatives -- including members of his family -- have been more keen for the forward to break records rather than focus on his long-term development.

articles.headline: State of each position in 2026: What are the biggest tactical trends?
articles.description: Elite soccer has changed dramatically in recent years, and the most valued player skill sets have evolved as a result.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年の各ポジションの現状：最大の戦術的トレンドとは？
articles.descriptionJa: エリートサッカーは近年劇的な変化を遂げており、その結果、最も価値の高い選手のスキルセットも進化している。
articles.body:
Elite European soccer in 2026 feels decidedly different from what we've become used to. Over the past couple of seasons, the Premier League has been increasingly characterized by direct attacking, set pieces and long throw-ins. Many encounters between big clubs across Europe have become frenetic, end-to-end affairs, such as the Bayern Munich-Paris Saint-Germain semifinals in last season's UEFA Champions League.

A lot of the changes seem related to how teams play without the ball. The soccer we became accustomed to throughout the 2010s involved top sides trying to push their opponents back while keeping the ball. Once the ball reached the attacking third, they tried to outnumber defenders in key spaces and make use of their attacking talent.

One way for defensive sides to counter this approach is to use zonal marking, which involves defending space rather than individual players. They would set up in compact blocks and deny space in critical areas, whether they defended deep like Max Allegri's Juventus in the 2010s or pressed high like teams coached by Ralf Rangnick's disciples. While this tactic helps protect the areas closer to goal and prevent mismatches, it sometimes plays into the hands of those high-possession sides.

As a result, player marking (or man-to-man marking), in which defenders are assigned to follow attackers around up and down the pitch, started to make a comeback at the turn of the 2020s. Teams like Mikel Arteta's Arsenal and Andoni Iraola's Bournemouth combined this concept with their zonal marking, switching out of a zonal structure in certain situations to swarm teams attempting to move the ball forward (hybrid pressing). This makes moving the ball slowly up the pitch harder, causing teams to embrace more direct approaches with the ball.

Meanwhile, the game appears to be becoming more physical and more intense. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, every passing season of the Premier League has seen faster sprinting and more "high-intensity actions." And with off-ball physical data like running distance or top speed becoming more accessible, scouting departments now possess more transparent measures of athleticism, leading to players' athletic qualities being valued more.

Rather than just affecting the head coach's team talk, these big-picture changes have a major effect on the skill sets that clubs look for when assembling their starting XIs. Let's take a look at five positions -- goalkeepers, center backs, fullbacks, central midfielders, and strikers -- to see what has changed and why.

Goalkeepers: Distribution and cross-claiming

New Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has generated much buzz this season. One of his standout features has been his passing ability, playing quick passes to his center backs during the early buildup and exquisite floated long passes to Villa's forwards to escape pressure.

articles.headline: How a mass Man City player exodus would warp the transfer market
articles.description: If Manchester City are punished by being relegated from the Premier League, group of players worth more than £1 billion in transfer fees would suddenly become available.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ選手の大量流出が移籍市場をどう激変させるか
articles.descriptionJa: もしマンチェスター・シティが罰則としてプレミアリーグから降格することになれば、総額10億ポンド以上の価値がある選手たちが突如として移籍市場に放出されることになる。
articles.body:
What would happen to the transfer market if a group of players worth over £1 billion suddenly became available in the same window, all anxious to immediately find a new club?

If Manchester City fail to overturn an independent commission finding that they were guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-season period -- City reject the findings and lodged their appeal on Oct. 2 -- the soccer world will find out exactly what it looks like when a collection of superstars and serial winners flood the market.

It would be a football version of "Supermarket Sweep" with Europe's biggest clubs raiding the Etihad Stadium for cut-price deals. With few exceptions, players would be ready to take the first opportunity to escape the crumbling empire they were once so desperate join.

But it would also distort the market more than any previous situation. Chelsea super-charged the transfer market when Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich funded their high spending in the mid-2000s. City took it to another level following Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan's takeover in 2008 -- that spending is the root of the problems they now find themselves in with the Premier League. But if the exit doors are forced open at the Etihad, it will drive transfer fees down and change the whole landscape of the market.

With Premier League CEO Richard Masters saying last week that City "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade," the likelihood is high of tough sanctions on the club if their appeal fails. Potential punishments include expulsion from the league -- City could be kicked out and forced to apply to rejoin at the bottom of the English football pyramid -- or a huge points deduction that would make relegation to the second-tier Championship unavoidable.

That outcome -- dropping down just one division -- might prove to be the best-case scenario for City. But don't be fooled into believing that the club would be able to ride it out, keep their squad intact and seal an instant return to the top division.

The financial implications of dropping out of the Premier League, and the Champions League, would be seismic even for a club of City's stature and the inevitable outcome would be a mass exodus of their high-earning players.

Championship clubs receive just £5.7 million a year from the EFL's broadcast deal. Last season, City banked £248.9 million in prize money (£165.5 million from the Premier League, £83.4 million from the Champions League), so a hole of more than £240 million would immediately appear in their finances.

City's most recently published wage bill, for the 2024-25 season, amounted to £408.4 million. It is now likely to be closer to an annual £450 million following the arrivals of players including Gianluigi Donnarumma, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernández.

articles.headline: Ledley King backs Tottenham form to 'turn around very quickly'
articles.description: Ledley King has urged Roberto De Zerbi's team to draw on the experiences of last season to end the club's winless start to the new Premier League campaign.
articles.headlineJa: レドリー・キング、トッテナムの調子は「すぐに好転する」と支持
articles.descriptionJa: レドリー・キングは、ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ率いるチームに対し、昨シーズンの経験を活かして、プレミアリーグ新シーズンでの勝ちなしスタートから脱却するよう促した。
articles.body:
Former Tottenham captain Ledley King has urged Roberto De Zerbi's team to draw on the experiences of last season to end the club's winless start to the new Premier League campaign.

Spurs have been bottom of the table since a 3-2 loss at home to Aston Villa on Sept. 19, which made it two points from five league matches.

After a summer of lavish spending following successive 17th-placed finishes, expectations were raised, but League Cup winner King believes one positive result can act as a catalyst for Tottenham to turn around their form.

The situation was far more bleak for Spurs in March when De Zerbi arrived in north London with the singular focus to avoid a catastrophic relegation to the Championship.

Even though confidence was at an all-time low, De Zerbi masterminded survival after a 15-match winless run in the division was snapped and King believes that experience can help before Saturday's trip to Manchester United.

"It's been tough at the moment, but you can see signs of improvement game by game," King said at a recent Hall of Fame event at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"[They have] no choice. You have to find a way. Most of the group have gone through difficult periods and they managed to find a way out last season.

"They'll have to draw on that to a certain degree, but there is no easy way. You keep working on the training pitch, keep putting the work in.

"It's just a confidence thing. These are top players. I'm sure once the first positive result goes for the team, things can turn around very quickly. Just keep working hard, keep believing in yourself. That's the only way to do it."

- Andrew Robertson after hitting 100 Scotland caps: Hopefully I can catch Kenny Dalglish

- Roberto De Zerbi receives backing of Tottenham's chief executive

- Jan Paul van Hecke returns to Tottenham after suffering foot injury with Netherlands

Former England centre back King spent his entire career at Tottenham and made 323 appearances despite a long-standing knee injury.

King etched his name into club folklore with League Cup success in 2008 and as captain during Spurs' first venture into the Champions League two years later.

After the 45-year-old was one of four people inducted into the relaunched Hall of Fame last month, he received a thunderous reception as a half-time guest for the Villa match.

King said: "To be in the Hall of Fame is really humbling."

articles.headline: Folarin Balogun reopens door to Premier League despite failed Everton move
articles.description: United States striker Folarin Balogun has said that he would still be keen to play in the Premier League, even though his transfer deadline day move to Everton collapsed in dramatic fashion.
articles.headlineJa: フォラリン・バログン、エバートンへの移籍失敗後もプレミアリーグ復帰に意欲
articles.descriptionJa: アメリカ代表ストライカーのフォラリン・バログンは、移籍期限最終日にエバートンへの移籍が劇的な形で崩れたものの、依然としてプレミアリーグでのプレーに意欲的であると語った。
articles.body:
United States striker Folarin Balogun has said that he would still be keen to play in the Premier League, even though his transfer deadline day move to Everton collapsed in dramatic fashion.

Balogun, 25, backed out of a move to the Toffees after Everton and Monaco started to restructure the terms of his transfer after issues were raised during the his medical examination at Everton's Finch Farm training ground.

Asked by talkSPORT if a Premier League move is something that he'd still be interested in, Balogun said: "Yes, potentially.

"Football has many twists and turns as we've seen after the World Cup.

"I was close to a transfer, didn't materialise, but for sure it's definitely an option."

Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro said at the time that Balogun abandoned the move due to concerns over his treatment by the Merseyside club.

The former Arsenal forward continues to play his football at Monaco, after a high-profile summer in which he put in some solid performances for the USMNT at the World Cup but also found himself the subject of a major controversy.

Balogun picked up a red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the round of 32 and was subsequently banned from the USMNT's round of 16 clash with Belgium.

But then, the red card and ban were overturned by FIFA after U.S. President Donald Trump asked FIFA chief Gianni Infantino to review the decision.

Infantino said the decision was not influenced by Trump. Balogun was handed a suspended ban that allowed him to play against Belgium, but the UMSNT lost and were eliminated from the tournament.

- Folarin Balogun red card U-turn 'most serious incident in the history of football' - LaLiga boss

- Pochettino shares 'regret' over Balogun controversy, impact on USMNT

- David Moyes vents over Everton transfer window after Folarin Balogun deal collapse

Monaco are flying high in Ligue 1 and currently sit at the top of the table after five games, five points ahead of reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain.

Balogun's first match back for Monaco after the summer's transfer debacle was against Lens. Monaco won 2-1.
